impact.why: The accounting bypass can weaken device or adapter monetary caps and permit additional billable operations under the victim user context.

likelihood.why: Adoption of lower-trust state, suitable orphan shape, existing gross spend, and later authorized online execution are all required.

limitations: A reclaim larger than gross spend triggers the existing fail-closed fallback.
The credit does not itself disclose secrets or send network traffic.
Independent folder, adapter, network, and secret controls can still block later work.

reachability.outcome: budget capacity can be reopened without a matching authentic reservation
reachability.summary: The attacker needs a supplied-state adoption path, a reclaimable failed online task shape, existing matching or device-wide gross spend, and later victim-authorized online work.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust contributor supplies an adopted store with a schema-valid failed online task carrying forged reservation fields. The victim runs indexing, KCS retires the orphan, appends a reclaim row, and later budget checks subtract the unsupported credit from genuine spend.

codeEvidence.code:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TaskDescriptor {
    pub task_id: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub task_type: TaskType,
    pub input_path: String,
    pub input_hash: String,
    pub output_ref: String,
    pub status: TaskStatus,
    pub fallback_reason: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub reserved_usd: Option<f64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub reserved_month: Option<String>,
}
codeEvidence.explanation: A supplied task record can carry `reserved_usd` and `reserved_month` as ordinary serialized fields alongside attacker-shaped task metadata.
codeEvidence.label: Task records carry mutable reservation stamps

codeEvidence.explanation: `TaskStore::all()` rejects out-of-scope paths and malformed hashes, but it does not bind reservation stamps to a trusted charge or reservation identity.
codeEvidence.label: Task loading checks path and hash shape only

codeEvidence.explanation: A schema-valid failed online task whose path is no longer live reaches `retire_online_task_reclaiming()` and can contribute a reclaim row.
codeEvidence.label: Index orphan sweep selects failed online tasks

codeEvidence.explanation: `reclaim_entry_for()` creates a positive reclaim credit from task-supplied amount and month without checking charge identity, provenance, or once-only consumption.
codeEvidence.label: Reclaim row copies amount and month from the task

codeEvidence.explanation: A forged reclaim amount that is finite and non-negative satisfies the shared ledger validation.
codeEvidence.label: Ledger validation accepts finite non-negative credits

codeEvidence.explanation: When the forged credit is smaller than unrelated gross spend, net spend remains non-negative and the credit lowers enforced spend.
codeEvidence.label: Budget enforcement subtracts reclaim credits from gross spend

remediation.summary: Bind every reclaim to one authentic prior reservation or charge identity and atomically consume that identity under the cost lock. Reject reservation-bearing task stamps that cannot be verified against the trusted ledger.
tests: Adopt a synthetic task with forged amount/month but no trusted reservation ID and assert no reclaim row is appended.
Verify one valid reservation can be reclaimed exactly once.
Reject duplicate, cross-scope, cross-adapter, and cross-month reservation claims.
Preserve the gross-spend fallback when reclaim exceeds gross spend.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that only KCS-issued, previously unmatched reservations may create reclaim credit. `TaskStore::all()` accepts serialized reservation stamps from task state after path and hash checks, and `reclaim_entry_for()` later copies those stamps into a positive device-global reclaim row without proving charge provenance or once-only use.

summary: KCS accepts reservation amount and month fields from persisted task records, converts selected failed orphan tasks into positive reclaim credits, and subtracts those credits from device-global spend without binding them to an authentic prior charge.
title: unbound reservation stamps can forge budget-reclaim credits

assertions: The task loader does not authenticate `reserved_usd` or `reserved_month` against a charge identity.
`reclaim_entry_for()` copies task amount and month into `MonthlyCostLedgerEntry` for eligible non-billable failures.
A forged credit below applicable gross spend lowers net spend and can reopen budget capacity.
limitations: No live adapter request or credential use was performed.
The attack requires lower-trust adopted or preseeded task state plus existing gross spend.
validation.method: static source trace plus local synthetic accounting probe
validation.summary: The source trace confirms that adopted task fields can carry reservation stamps, the orphan-reclaim path converts them into reclaim rows, and net spend subtracts accepted credits. The local PoC reproduced the accounting effect with synthetic rows only.
